definitions.gloss: familiarity from hearing, recognition by ear
definitions.explanation: The sense that one has heard something before — a voice, a name, a melody, or a phrase. Used when something sounds familiar even if one cannot pinpoint when or where it was heard.

examples.japanese: {聞|き}き{覚|おぼ}えのある{声|こえ}だった。
examples.english: It was a voice I recognized.

examples.japanese: その{名前|なまえ}には{聞|き}き{覚|おぼ}えがある。
examples.english: That name sounds familiar to me.

examples.japanese: {聞|き}き{覚|おぼ}えのあるメロディーが{流|なが}れてきて、{懐|なつ}かしい{気持|きも}ちになった。
examples.english: A familiar melody started playing, and I felt nostalgic.

notes:
USAGE:
The most common patterns are {聞|き}き{覚|おぼ}えがある (to sound familiar / to recognize from hearing) and {聞|き}き{覚|おぼ}えのある + noun (a familiar-sounding ~). The negative {聞|き}き{覚|おぼ}えがない means something is not familiar at all.

Compare with the visual equivalent {見覚|みおぼ}え (recognition by sight / visual familiarity).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {聞|き}き{覚|おぼ}えがある: to sound familiar
- {聞|き}き{覚|おぼ}えがない: to not sound familiar at all
- {聞|き}き{覚|おぼ}えのある{声|こえ}: a familiar voice
- {聞|き}き{覚|おぼ}えのある{名前|なまえ}: a familiar-sounding name
